::: {#thm-negate-quantifiers}
#### Negating a quantifier

For a set $S$ and a predicate $P(x)$ (@def-predicate) whose domain (@def-domain) is $S$:

1. $\neg (\forall x \in S, P(x))$ and $\exists x \in S, \neg P(x)$ have the same truth value;
2. $\neg (\exists x \in S, P(x))$ and $\forall x \in S, \neg P(x)$ have the same truth value.

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

1. By @def-universal-quantifier,
   $\forall x \in S, P(x)$ is false exactly when $P(x)$ is false for at least one $x$ in $S$,
   which by @def-existential-quantifier is when $\exists x \in S, \neg P(x)$ is true.
2. By @def-existential-quantifier,
   $\exists x \in S, P(x)$ is false exactly when $P(x)$ is false for every $x$ in $S$,
   which by @def-universal-quantifier is when $\forall x \in S, \neg P(x)$ is true.

:::

:::
